subject: octopus
pitch: A curious reef octopus in coral and rust tones, covered in little bumps and paler mottling. A soft, bulbous head, golden eyes with bar-shaped pupils and a slightly grumpy brow. Its eight arms curl out in every direction, each lined with rows of cream suckers, and one arm proudly holds up an old brass key it found on a shipwreck.
reasoning:
I need to build a TypeScript module using the SDK, sticking closely to the documented API surface like createBuilder and the joint method with its at/aim/dir/up parameters, keeping things concise but functional.

Working through chains, sweeps, lofts, and limb-building primitives like sprout and spike, I'm uncertain about exact parameter signatures for things like sweep radius or loft stations, so I'll make reasonable assumptions and keep usage consistent -- for arms I'll build a chain from catmull points, then sweep it with an assumed radius option, accepting the risk of guessing at the exact signature.

For eyes and other simple parts, I'll fall back on plain THREE.js geometry combined with b.stick to keep things safe. Surfaces I'll derive from bodies using b.surface with nearest/around/ray methods, and for coloring I'll skip the uncertain paint/spots/stripes functions entirely and just pass color strings directly into stick and sweep calls.

For the brass key, instead of risking an unfamiliar extrude API I'll build it from basic torus and box geometries attached via b.stick to a hand joint, trusting the joint-to-frame conversion to orient it naturally. For the arm suckers, I'll use b.along over the arm's path array to place small spheres at intervals along each tentacle.

Now I'm structuring the octopus builder itself: a head joint anchors a scaled sphere for the bulbous mantle, since true lofting seems overkill, and I'm working out how to attach eye spheres onto the head's surface using a returned mesh handle from the stick call.

Now planning the eight arms radiating from the mantle base, generating each as a curling catmull-rom path with angular spacing and some randomized jitter, then sweeping them into tapered tubes. For suckers, I'll place small spheres along each arm chain using an "along" helper that walks the path and seats items at tangent-aligned frames, accepting the rough placement on the underside for now.

For texture, I'm scattering tiny bump spheres across the head surface using a scatter helper, uncertain of its exact signature but planning to call it with just a count. For the signature key arm, I'm raising its tip and attaching a key shape there built from a torus bow, box shaft, and teeth — since stick only takes a single geometry, I'll assemble the key from multiple separate stick calls rather than merging geometries into one group.

I'm defining the color palette as hex strings for coral, rust, pale tan, cream, gold, brass, and dark pupil, then planning the mottled skin texture with flattened pale spheres via the scatter approach. For ground placement, I'm working out vertical offsets so the mantle and curling arms all stay above y=0, sketching rough radius and center-height values to keep everything resting naturally on the floor, then starting to write a helper function that generates arm point paths using angle and randomness per arm index.

Still writing arm point generation...

Now I'm placing the eyes on the head sphere using nearest-surface hits, adding gold eye spheres with dark bar-shaped pupils pushed slightly outward to avoid clipping, then angled brow boxes that rotate inward differently depending on left or right side, and finally scattering small bumps across the head surface.

I'm reconsidering the head construction itself—realizing a simple catmull tube sweep gives uniform radius and won't produce the bulbous shape I want, so I need a different approach, maybe shaping it as a tapered capsule-like sweep with rising control points even though the exact tapering/cap behavior of the sweep function is uncertain.

Working out placement: arms should attach near the base of the head around y=0.2-0.3, and I'm adjusting the head sweep's starting height so its bottom doesn't dip below the floor while keeping total octopus height around 0.84-0.9, which feels proportionate. I'm also planning the joint structure—a root "mantle" joint plus arm chains built via a chain helper that lays out joints along a path—and setting up a seeded random generator for variation before writing the actual code.
